newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Banned Nobel laureate still wants to visit Manila.
newsitem.headline: Banned Nobel laureate still wants to visit Manila.

text.p: Nobel Peace Prize winner and East Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, banned by Manila from visiting the country during next month's APEC summit, said he would like to visit the Philippines next year.

"I welcome the suggestion made by some members of your government that I visit the Philippines on another occasion. I intend to do so next January on a teaching assignment," Ramos-Horta said in a letter dated November 2 to Philippine President Fidel Ramos.
The letter was released on Monday by human rights activists in the Philippines.

Ramos-Horta was invited to speak on East Timor at an international conference of non-governmental organisations to be held in parallel with the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit scheduled on November 25.
But the Philippines banned him from entering the country saying his presence might disrupt the APEC meeting.
One of the leaders expected to attend the summit is Indonesian President Suharto.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the next year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
The East Timorese resistance leader, who lives in Sydney, said he planned to visit Manila next January provided there is "no legal or administrative bar" to his entry.

"I would like to assure you Mr President that I can fully understand your present situation regarding my presence in your country, and I am confident that under other circumstances a visit of mine to the Philippines would not constitute a problem for you," Ramos-Horta said.
Government spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
Ramos-Horta won the Nobel prize jointly with the Bishop of Timor Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo.
